title: Contracted Seats and Their Assignment — Corporate Travel Programmes
content:
The contracted seats are placed on the programme for each contract period, and a seat is consumed the moment it is assigned to a named traveller. The seat allowance of a programme under the Corporate Travel Programmes is accordingly the contracted traveller seats still unassigned on it: a grant for the contract period adds to it, and each assignment to a named traveller takes one away.

**The state the programme must stand in.** A seat is assigned only while the programme record stands at active. The standing that answers this is the one the programme's own record shows for the programme the seat belongs to, read before the assignment, and active is the only standing at which a seat is assigned.

**The authority behind a seat change.** Seats are changed only when the corporate desk has already recorded an approved seat request against this programme. The authority is the seat request's own recorded standing, correlated to the change by the request it was raised under and read before the change; what the administrator says about an approval does not answer it.

**Moving a seat between travellers.** A seat may be moved from one traveller to another only after it has been held for the tier's cool-off days, and the move carries the tier's reassignment charge.

**Seats changed mid-term.** Seats added mid-term are charged at the tier's seat licence rate pro rata for the remainder of the period, and seats removed mid-term are not credited until the next period begins.

**A traveller without a seat.** A traveller without an assigned seat may not book through the programme at all, and a booking attempted for them is refused rather than charged at the public price.

**Seats do not travel.** Seats never move between programmes, not even between entities of the same group.

## The cool-off read on both of its sides

The cool-off is counted in the calendar days published for the tier, and it runs on the seat's being held by the traveller it is being moved from.

| How long the seat has been held | Standing of a move to another traveller |
| --- | --- |
| Fewer days than the tier's cool-off days | The seat is not moved |
| The tier's cool-off days, reached | The seat may be moved, and the move carries the tier's reassignment charge |
| More than the tier's cool-off days | The seat may be moved, and the move carries the tier's reassignment charge |

On a tier whose published cool-off is 0 calendar days there is no period to wait out; on a tier whose published cool-off is 90 calendar days the seat is held that long before it moves. The reassignment charge follows the tier in the same way, and on a tier whose published charge is nil the move carries nothing.

## Notes on the seat allowance

- A seat that has been granted but not yet assigned to a named traveller is still part of the programme's unassigned seat allowance.
- A seat removed part way through a period is credited from the beginning of the next period and not before.
- A group of companies holding several programmes cannot move a seat from one of them to another; each programme keeps its own seats.
